x: Andy LeHeron, now a member of Belgrave finished in a good 58:57 to take second handicap award

A touch of the old one two as Carl and Alan fought out the premier placings with Carl getting the edge - just. Andy LeHeron showed excellent form to be the first Junior home - what a prospect this tall Channel Islander could be.

A specially arranged sharpener before the National '10' gave Tommy Cook the opportunity to romp away with the prize closely pursued by Johnny Morris and John Keown. Wilf Wesch was the fastest man of the day although Ray Middleton, John Moullin and Andy LeHeron were also impressive.
